entities.blurb: An eyeblossom is a unique flower found in the pale garden biome. It changes state depending on the daylight cycle, closing during the day and opening at night. Its "eye", visible only when the flower is open, glows in the dark but does not emit light in its surroundings.

entities.blurb: A block of coal, also known as a coal block, is a storage block, equivalent to nine coal, that can also be used as fuel.

entities.blurb:

entities.blurb: Coarse dirt is a variant of dirt which grass blocks cannot spread to.

entities.blurb: Cobbled deepslate is a stone variant that functions similar to cobblestone or blackstone.

entities.blurb: A cobblestone slab is a decorative slab variant of cobblestone that generates in overworld structures and is used for building.

entities.blurb: A cobweb is a block that drastically slows down the movement of most entities touching it. The Weaving effect lessens this movement speed decrease.
entities.name: Cobweb

entities.blurb:
Cocoa beans are items obtained from cocoa pods, and are used to plant more of them as well as to craft brown dye and cookies.
Cocoa pods are plant blocks that can only be placed on jungle log sides and grow cocoa beans. They can be found naturally in jungles.
entities.name: Cocoa

entities.blurb:
A command block is an indestructible block that can execute commands. Because it cannot be obtained, destroyed or used in Survival mode without cheats, it is primarily used in multiplayer servers, Creative worlds, and custom maps. There are 3 types of these blocks.
An impulse command block is the default block type; it executes only once when activated.
A chain command block executes every time when triggered.
A repeating command block executes every game tick as long as it is activated.
entities.name: Command Block

entities.blurb: A redstone comparator is a block that can compare the strength of two different redstone signals or subtract one from the other. It can also read the fullness of containers and the state of a few selected blocks.
entities.name: Redstone Comparator

entities.blurb: A composter is a block that converts some biological material into bone meal. It also serves as a farmer's job site block.
entities.name: Composter

entities.blurb: A conduit is a block that can be placed underwater and surrounded by prismarine to activate it. Once active, it empowers nearby players touching water or rain, prevents them from drowning, and attacks wet monsters.
entities.name: Conduit

entities.blurb: Copper bars are copper variants of bars. Unlike iron bars, they are colored copper orange and can oxidize over time, similar to other copper blocks.
entities.name: Copper Bars

entities.blurb: A block of copper, internally known as a copper block, is a block that oxidizes over time, gaining a verdigris appearance over four stages. They can be prevented from oxidizing by being waxed with honeycombs. Non-oxidized blocks of copper are storage blocks equivalent to nine copper ingots.
entities.name: Block of Copper

entities.blurb:
A copper bulb is a light-emitting block. It toggles on or off when it receives a redstone pulse, and does not need continuous power to emit light. Its light level depends on its state of oxidation.
Waxed copper bulbs do not oxidize, but otherwise function identically.
entities.name: Copper Bulb

entities.blurb: A copper chain is an oxidizing directional block and the copper variant of chains.
entities.name: Copper Chain

entities.blurb:
A copper chest is a type of chest made of copper. It functions almost identically to a normal wooden chest, except that it oxidizes over time, and copper golems remove items from it to store inside nearby wooden chests.
Like normal chests, two copper chests can merge into a large copper chest if placed adjacent each other.
entities.name: Copper Chest

entities.blurb: The copper door is a type of door made of copper that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
entities.name: Copper Door

entities.blurb: A copper golem statue is the result of a copper golem fully oxidizing and petrifying into a block. It can be posed in four different ways, or it can be reanimated by scraping it with an axe enough times.
entities.name: Copper Golem Statue

entities.blurb: Copper grates are a variant of copper blocks that have perforations that can be seen through.
entities.name: Copper Grate

entities.blurb: A copper lantern is a copper variant of a lantern that displays a green flame and oxidizes over time.
entities.name: Copper Lantern

entities.blurb:
Copper ore is an ore block found underground.
Deepslate copper ore is the deepslate variant of copper ore, usually found deeper underground.
entities.name: Copper Ore

entities.blurb: A copper torch is a non-solid block that emits light. Copper torches can also be used to craft copper lanterns.
entities.name: Copper Torch

entities.blurb: A copper trapdoor is a type of trapdoor made from copper that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone. A copper trapdoor can exist in one of eight variants depending on how oxidized it is and whether it is waxed or not.
entities.name: Copper Trapdoor

entities.blurb: A copper torch is a non-solid block that emits light. Copper torches can also be used to craft copper lanterns.

entities.blurb: Cracked polished blackstone bricks are the cracked variant of polished blackstone bricks.

entities.blurb: Cracked stone bricks are a variant of stone bricks, obtained through smelting and natural generation.

entities.blurb: A crafter is a low-capacity storage block that can use its contents to craft items when given a redstone signal, ejecting the results into the world or into a container it is facing. Its inventory slots can be individually locked so hoppers and similar blocks cannot fill them, while not affecting crafting recipes.

entities.blurb: A crafting table is a utility block that gives access to all crafting recipes, including many not available from the inventory's crafting grid.
entities.name: Crafting Table

entities.blurb: A creaking heart is a living block that can be crafted or found in pale oak trees in pale gardens. It activates if placed in a line between two pale oak logs; then, during nighttime, it spawns a creaking and protects it from all damage. Breaking a creaking heart that is protecting a creaking instantly kills it. Hitting a protected creaking causes resin clumps to grow on pale oak logs near its linked creaking heart.
entities.name: Creaking Heart

entities.blurb: A creeper head is the head of a creeper in the form of a block. It can only be obtained by killing a creeper using a different charged creeper's explosion.

entities.blurb: A hanging sign is a variant of a  sign that displays text, and can be placed underneath blocks or with a solid self-supporting bracket. The text of hanging signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent edits.

entities.blurb: Wood or hyphae is a block that has the log's "bark" texture on all six sides. It comes in 12 types: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, crimson, warped, pale oak, and poplar.

entities.blurb: Crimson nylium is a variant of netherrack that generates in the Nether.

entities.blurb:
A cake is a block that can serve as food. It can be eaten by placing and using it, with each use consuming one of its seven slices. The entire cake gives the most hunger points out of every food item, but has low saturation.

entities.blurb: A decorated pot is a storage block crafted from bricks and/or pottery sherds, with the items used individually affecting the appearance of its four side faces. It can store a single inventory slot's worth of items, which cannot be seen or retrieved by hand without breaking the pot.
entities.name: Decorated Pot

entities.blurb: Deepslate is a stone type found deep underground in the Overworld that functions similarly to regular stone, but takes significantly longer to mine.
entities.name: Deepslate

entities.blurb: A deepslate brick slab is a decorative slab variant of deepslate bricks that generates in ancient cities and is used for building.
entities.name: Deepslate Brick Slab

entities.blurb: Deepslate brick stairs are a decorative stairs variant of deepslate bricks that generate in ancient cities and are used for building.
entities.name: Deepslate Brick Stairs

entities.blurb: A deepslate brick wall is a decorative wall variant of deepslate bricks that generates in ancient cities and is used for building.
entities.name: Deepslate Brick Wall

entities.blurb: Deepslate bricks are the brick variant of deepslate.
entities.name: Deepslate Bricks

entities.blurb:
Coal ore is a mineral block that drops coal when mined.
Deepslate coal ore is a variant of coal ore that rarely generates at the top of the deepslate layer and around sulfur springs.
entities.name: Deepslate Coal Ore

entities.blurb:
Copper ore is an ore block found underground.
Deepslate copper ore is the deepslate variant of copper ore, usually found deeper underground.
entities.name: Deepslate Copper Ore

entities.blurb:
Diamond ore is a rare ore that generates deep underground, and drops diamonds when mined.
Deepslate diamond ore is a variant of diamond ore that can generate in deepslate and tuff blobs, and is more common than its regular variant.
entities.name: Deepslate Diamond Ore

entities.blurb:
Emerald ore is a rare mineral block that generates only in mountains and windswept hills biomes. It drops emeralds when mined, or itself if mined with a pickaxe with the Silk Touch enchantment.
Deepslate emerald ore is a rare variant of emerald ore that can generate in deepslate and tuff blobs.
entities.name: Deepslate Emerald Ore

entities.blurb:
Gold ore is a rare mineral block found underground that drops raw gold when mined with an iron pickaxe or better.
Deepslate gold ore is a variant of gold ore that can generate in deepslate and tuff.
entities.name: Deepslate Gold Ore

entities.blurb:
Iron ore is a mineral block typically found underground. It is a source of raw iron, which can be smelted into iron ingots. 
Deepslate iron ore is the deepslate variant of iron ore. It is found in deepslate layers.
entities.name: Deepslate Iron Ore

entities.blurb:
Lapis lazuli ore, internally known as lapis ore, is the ore block from which lapis lazuli is obtained.
Deepslate lapis lazuli ore, internally known as deepslate lapis ore, is a variant of lapis lazuli ore that generates in deepslate layers.
entities.name: Deepslate Lapis Lazuli Ore

entities.blurb:
Redstone ore is the ore block from which redstone dust is obtained.
Deepslate redstone ore is a variant of redstone ore that can generate in deepslate and tuff blobs.
entities.name: Deepslate Redstone Ore

entities.blurb: A deepslate tile slab is a decorative slab variant of deepslate tiles that generates in ancient cities and is used for building.
entities.name: Deepslate Tile Slab

entities.blurb: Deepslate tile stairs are a decorative stairs variant of deepslate tiles that generate in ancient cities and are used for building.
entities.name: Deepslate Tile Stairs

entities.blurb: A deepslate tile wall is a decorative wall variant of deepslate tiles that generates in ancient cities and is used for building.
entities.name: Deepslate Tile Wall

entities.blurb: Deepslate tiles are a decorative variant of deepslate.
entities.name: Deepslate Tiles

entities.blurb: The detector rail is a type of rail that produces a redstone signal while a minecart is on it.
entities.name: Detector Rail

entities.blurb: A block of diamond, known internally as a diamond block, is a precious mineral block equivalent to nine diamonds.
entities.name: Block of Diamond

entities.blurb:
Diamond ore is a rare ore that generates deep underground, and drops diamonds when mined.
Deepslate diamond ore is a variant of diamond ore that can generate in deepslate and tuff blobs, and is more common than its regular variant.
entities.name: Diamond Ore

entities.blurb: Diorite is a block of igneous rock, found in large pockets underground.
entities.name: Diorite

entities.blurb: A diorite slab is a decorative slab variant of diorite that generates in snowy villages and is used for building.
entities.name: Diorite Slab

entities.blurb: Diorite stairs are a decorative stairs variant of diorite that generate in snowy tundra villages and are used for building.
entities.name: Diorite Stairs

entities.blurb: A diorite wall is a decorative wall variant of diorite that generates in snowy tundra villages and is used for building.
entities.name: Diorite Wall

entities.blurb: Dirt is a block found abundantly in most biomes under a layer of grass blocks at the top of the Overworld as well as in patches underground.
entities.name: Dirt

entities.blurb: Dirt paths are decorative blocks created by using a shovel on most types of dirt. They are mainly found in villages as a path for the villagers.
entities.name: Dirt Path

entities.blurb: A dispenser is a low-capacity storage block that can fire projectiles, use certain items and tools, as well as place certain blocks, fluids, or entities when given a redstone signal. Items that do not have unique dispenser functions are instead ejected into the world like a dropper.
entities.name: Dispenser

entities.blurb: The dragon egg is a gravity-affected block that can be obtained only once per world (or twice in Bedrock Edition) by defeating the ender dragon. It teleports to avoid being mined, but drops as an item if it falls onto a non-full block such as a torch or is pushed by a piston.
entities.name: Dragon Egg

entities.blurb: A dragon head is a block that resembles a smaller version of the ender dragon's head. It can only be obtained from End ships.
entities.name: Dragon Head

entities.blurb: A dragon head is a block that resembles a smaller version of the ender dragon's head. It can only be obtained from End ships.
entities.name: Dragon Wall Head

entities.blurb: A dried ghast is an immobile, shriveled, harmless ghast in the form of a block. It can be found near Nether fossils, obtained through bartering, or crafted. Placing it in water causes it to hydrate over time until it becomes a ghastling.
entities.name: Dried Ghast

entities.blurb: Dried kelp blocks are storage blocks equivalent to nine dried kelp. They can also be used as fuel.
entities.name: Dried Kelp Block

entities.blurb: Dripstone block is a rock block that allows pointed dripstone to grow beneath it if there is water on top of it.
entities.name: Dripstone Block

entities.blurb: A dropper is a low-capacity storage block that can eject its contents into the world or into other containers when given a redstone signal.
entities.name: Dropper

entities.blurb: A block of emerald, internally known as an emerald block, is a mineral block equivalent to nine emeralds.
entities.name: Block of Emerald

entities.blurb:
Emerald ore is a rare mineral block that generates only in mountains and windswept hills biomes. It drops emeralds when mined, or itself if mined with a pickaxe with the Silk Touch enchantment.
Deepslate emerald ore is a rare variant of emerald ore that can generate in deepslate and tuff blobs.
entities.name: Emerald Ore

entities.blurb: An enchanting table is a block used to spend experience and lapis lazuli to apply enchantments to tools, armor and books. Surrounding it with up to fifteen bookshelves increases both its enchanting power and level requirement.
entities.name: Enchanting Table

entities.blurb:
The End gateway is a block that forms a part of End gateways, which teleport the player between the central island and the outer islands in the End.
It is one of two blocks that use the starfield effect.
entities.name: End Gateway

entities.blurb:
The End portal block is a block generated when an End portal or exit portal is activated, which teleports the player between the Overworld and the End.
It is one of two blocks that use the starfield effect.
entities.name: End Portal

entities.blurb: An End portal frame is an indestructible block, 12 of which form an End portal. Eyes of ender must be inserted into all 12 empty frames (if not already present upon generation) for the portal to activate and allow passage into the End dimension.
entities.name: End Portal Frame

entities.blurb: An End rod is a decorative light source that emits white particles.
entities.name: End Rod

entities.blurb: End stone is a block that appears in the End, and apart from generated structures, makes up all of the solid ground that exists in that dimension.
entities.name: End Stone

entities.blurb: An End stone brick slab is a decorative slab variant of End stone bricks that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
entities.name: End Stone Brick Slab

entities.blurb: End stone brick stairs are a decorative stairs variant of End stone bricks that do not generate naturally and are used for building.
entities.name: End Stone Brick Stairs

entities.blurb: An End stone brick wall is a decorative wall variant of End stone bricks that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
entities.name: End Stone Brick Wall

entities.blurb: End stone bricks are decorative building blocks made of End stone that generate in End cities.
entities.name: End Stone Bricks

entities.blurb: An ender chest is a type of chest whose contents are exclusive to each player, and they can be placed and accessed from anywhere in any dimension.
entities.name: Ender Chest

entities.blurb: Chiseled copper is a variant of copper blocks that generates in trial chambers.
entities.name: Exposed Chiseled Copper

entities.blurb: A block of copper, internally known as a copper block, is a block that oxidizes over time, gaining a verdigris appearance over four stages. They can be prevented from oxidizing by being waxed with honeycombs. Non-oxidized blocks of copper are storage blocks equivalent to nine copper ingots.
entities.name: Exposed Copper

entities.blurb: Copper bars are copper variants of bars. Unlike iron bars, they are colored copper orange and can oxidize over time, similar to other copper blocks.
entities.name: Exposed Copper Bars

entities.blurb:
A copper bulb is a light-emitting block. It toggles on or off when it receives a redstone pulse, and does not need continuous power to emit light. Its light level depends on its state of oxidation.
Waxed copper bulbs do not oxidize, but otherwise function identically.
entities.name: Exposed Copper Bulb

entities.blurb: A copper chain is an oxidizing directional block and the copper variant of chains.
entities.name: Exposed Copper Chain

entities.blurb:
A copper chest is a type of chest made of copper. It functions almost identically to a normal wooden chest, except that it oxidizes over time, and copper golems remove items from it to store inside nearby wooden chests.
Like normal chests, two copper chests can merge into a large copper chest if placed adjacent each other.
entities.name: Exposed Copper Chest

entities.blurb: The copper door is a type of door made of copper that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
entities.name: Exposed Copper Door

entities.blurb: A copper golem statue is the result of a copper golem fully oxidizing and petrifying into a block. It can be posed in four different ways, or it can be reanimated by scraping it with an axe enough times.
entities.name: Exposed Copper Golem Statue

entities.blurb: Copper grates are a variant of copper blocks that have perforations that can be seen through.
entities.name: Exposed Copper Grate

entities.blurb: A copper lantern is a copper variant of a lantern that displays a green flame and oxidizes over time.
entities.name: Exposed Copper Lantern

entities.blurb: A copper trapdoor is a type of trapdoor made from copper that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone. A copper trapdoor can exist in one of eight variants depending on how oxidized it is and whether it is waxed or not.
entities.name: Exposed Copper Trapdoor
